ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In 2010, China's industrial added value increased by 12.1% year-on-year. Read the figure and answer: <image1> What still needs to be improved to be able to promote the sustainable growth of China's industrial output value?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a combined bar and line chart of “2006—2010 total industrial added value and its growth rate.” The bar data indicate that China's total industrial added value generally increased; the line shows that the growth rate fluctuated, dropping approximately from 12.9% and 14.9% to 9.9% and 8.7%, and then rising again to 12.1% in 2010. Then reason: The question stem asks “what still needs to be improved to be able to promote the sustainable growth of China's industrial output value.” The growth rate in the figure did not continuously increase, indicating that simply pursuing the expansion of output value scale or short-term growth rate cannot necessarily guarantee sustainable growth. To achieve long-term stable growth, it is necessary to improve the quality and efficiency of industrial production, so industrial production benefits should be improved.
